Bulgarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

By surface analysis, у́там (útam, “to hoot”) +‎ -ка (-ka), probably of onomatopoeic origin.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈutkɐ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -utkɐ
  • Syllabification(key): ут‧ка

Noun

[edit]

у́тка • (útka) f (masculine ут) (dialectal)

  1. (literally) hooter
  2. a type of bird
    1. (Western dialects) female equivalent of ут (ut): owl, strix
      Synonyms: со́ва (sóva), у́лулица (úlulica)
    2. (Eastern dialects) various waterfowl such as types of anatids or shags

[edit]

útko 		у́тки

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ху́тка (hútka), ву́тка (vútka)

Related terms

[edit]
  • у́тица (útica) (with suffix -ица (-ica))

References

[edit]
  • Nayden Gerov; Тодор Панчев (1904), “у́тка”, in Рѣчникъ на Блъгарскꙑй язꙑкъ. Съ тлъкувание рѣчи-тꙑ на Блъгарскꙑ и на Русскꙑ. [Dictionary of the Bulgarian language] (in Bulgarian), volume 5, Plovdiv: Дружествена печꙗтница "Съгласие.", page 461

Komi-Zyrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian утка (utka).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈutka/, [ˈutkä]
  • Rhymes: -utka
  • Hyphenation: ут‧ка

Noun

[edit]

утка • (utka)

  1. duck (small bird of the family Anatidae)

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫtъka, equivalent to Proto-Slavic *ǫty +‎ -ка (-ka).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈutka]

Noun

[edit]

утка • (utka) f

  1. owl
  2. something incorrectly chosen or assumed
  3. situation where something is incorrectly chosen or assumed
  4. someone who incorrectly chooses or assumes

Declension

[edit]
Declension of утка
singular plural
indefinite утка (utka) утки (utki)
definite unspecified утката (utkata) утките (utkite)
definite proximal уткава (utkava) уткиве (utkive)
definite distal уткана (utkana) уткине (utkine)
vocative утко (utko) утки (utki)

Synonyms

[edit]
  • ут (ut)
  • був (buv)

Old Ruthenian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ꙋ́тка (útka), ву́тъка (vútka)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic у́тъка (útŭka), from Proto-Slavic *ǫ̀tъka. Cognate with Russian у́тка (útka).

Noun

[edit]

утка • (utka) f animal

  1. duck

Descendants

[edit]
  • Belarusian: ву́тка (vútka)
  • Ukrainian: у́тка (útka), ву́тка (vútka)

Further reading

[edit]
  • Bulyka, A. M., editor (2015), “утка, вутка”, in Гістарычны слоўнік беларускай мовы [Historical Dictionary of the Belarusian Language] (in Belarusian), numbers 35 (уморати – фолдровый), Minsk: Belaruskaia navuka, →ISBN, page 276

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
утка
Wikipedia ru

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic ꙋтъка (utŭka), from Proto-Slavic *ǫtъka, diminutive of *ǫty. By surface analysis, уть (utʹ) +‎ -ка (-ka). Cognate to Lithuanian antis, Latin anas.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈutkə]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

у́тка • (útka) f anim (genitive у́тки, nominative plural у́тки, genitive plural у́ток, relational adjective ути́ный, diminutive у́точка)

  1. duck (also as a food)
    Она́ прожо́рлива, как у́тка ― Oná prožórliva, kak útka ― She's as gluttonous as a pig (literally, “She's as gluttonous as a duck.”)
    • 1869, Лев Толстой [Leo Tolstoy], “Том 2, Часть пятая, XI”, in Война и мир; English translation from Aylmer and Louise Maude, transl., War and Peace, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1922–1923:
      Он был убеждён, что как у́тка сотворена́ так, что она́ всегда́ должна́ жить в воде́, так и он сотворён Бо́гом так, что до́лжен жить в три́дцать ты́сяч дохо́да и занима́ть всегда́ вы́сшее положе́ние в о́бществе.
      On byl ubeždjón, što kak útka sotvorená tak, što oná vsegdá dolžná žitʹ v vodé, tak i on sotvorjón Bógom tak, što dólžen žitʹ v trídcatʹ týsjač doxóda i zanimátʹ vsegdá výsšeje položénije v óbščestve.
      He was convinced that, as a duck is so made that it must live in water, so God had made him such that he must spend thirty thousand rubles a year and always occupy a prominent position in society.
  2. canard
  3. bed urinal
  4. (technology) cleat
    Synonym: крепи́тельная у́тка (krepítelʹnaja útka)
  5. (ironic, figuratively) clumsy woman
  6. (colloquial, journalism) deliberately implausible news or sensations; tabloidism
    Synonym: газе́тная у́тка (gazétnaja útka)
